simulation_method.value: Density Functional Theory (DFT) ab-initio calculations (Hohenberg-Kohn formalism)

potential_model_or_database.value: GGA Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) exchange-correlation functional, spin-polarized; ultrasoft pseudo-potentials based on modified Rappe-Rabe-Kaxiras-Joannopoulos (RRKJ) scheme

boundary_and_initial_conditions.value: Brillouin zone integration with an 18×18×18 Monkhorst-Pack grid for structure optimization; real-space grid with 50 Ryd energy cut-off for charge density; augmentation charges expanded to 600 Ryd; a 30×30×30 grid with 60 Ryd cut-off used for electronic density of states and formation energy calculations; bulk modulus obtained by fitting simulated unit-cell volumes with a Murnaghan equation of state; dynamical matrices from linear response in the harmonic approximation; density of states by the tetrahedron method with a 30×30×30 mesh.

validation_against_experiment.value: Calculated lattice parameters of ordered precipitates (e.g. FeAl-B2) were slightly less than experimental values but in good agreement; the calculated lattice constant of Fe3AlC was larger than Fe3Al-L12, matching experimental observations; enrichment of κ-phase with Mn increased calculated bulk/shear/Young's moduli, consistent with the experimentally observed increase in hardness.

model_name.value: Sound velocity relations for elastic constants

equation_role.value: Used elastic constants C11 and C44 from the slope of acoustic branches in the [100] direction and C12 from the [111] direction (equations 1–3)
Orthorhombic and monoclinic lattice distortions used to determine C11, C12 and C44 from total-energy changes (equations 4–7)

model_note.value: E(δ)=E(0)+(C11−C12)Vδ^2+O(δ^4) for orthorhombic distortion; E(δ)=E(0)+½C44Vδ^2+O(δ^4) for monoclinic distortion.

equation_role.value: Computed bulk modulus B0, anisotropy factor C_a, shear modulus G and Young's moduli E100 and E111 (equations 8–12)
Rationalized increased hardness from nano-sized disc-like B2 in α: the increase in shear stress (Δτ) is proportional to the inverse of the precipitate diameter (Δτ ∝ R^−1.25)

model_note.value: Smaller precipitate size increases resistance to shear, explaining higher hardness at higher annealing temperatures.

unmapped_findings: For the Ni-free alloy at 900 °C the Al content of the B2 particles in α (nanosized B2) was ~22.9 wt.% and of the coarse FeAl-type B2 particles in γ was ~18.3 wt.%; b0029 states the Al content of the particles ranged from 22.8 to 24.6 wt.% for the 900–1050 °C treatments.

The nanoindentation technique used in this study could not measure isolated nano-sized precipitates; it measured a compound hardness of the matrix together with the nano-sized features (compound values), so individual nano-particle hardness could not be resolved (b0026, b0042).

The coarse B2 phase formed in γ was reported with flat interfaces and sharp edges with an average size of ≈1.4 μm (b0026), whereas Table 1 lists coarse B2 particles of 2–4 μm for the Ni-free alloy at 900 °C (b0022).
The annealing holding time for the 900 °C treatment is not explicitly reported in the paper (b0017).
The paper labels the same Ni-free alloy both as Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C (text) and as Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.5C (Tables 1 and 2), an apparent typographical inconsistency (b0017, b0022, b0032).
